stories.title: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, starting with cyber defenders
paragraphs: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct. 28, calling it its strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. It arrives two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google says Carbon ranks first on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59 and reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching.

According to Google, internal teams have seen Carbon work for days on multi-step engineering tasks, and its success rate at generating secure code is more than double Argon's. MarkTechPost notes these are Google's own or self-run figures, with most rival scores self-reported and no independent replication yet.

Access is limited for now. Google is taking part in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release testing, is giving Carbon to a subset of cyber defenders this week, and will widen access through its Fairwind Program before a later release to developers, businesses and consumers. Introductory pricing matches Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

stories.title: Mistral releases the open weights of Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter model it calls the best open model for coding
paragraphs: Mistral AI released the weights of Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, on Oct. 29, 2026, the company announced. Mistral describes it as its flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, first released in public preview earlier in October, and says it was trained from scratch on European infrastructure. The model is free to use, modify, fine-tune and commercialize under a modified MIT license, except that companies offering it as a hosted model service need a separate commercial license.

Mistral says three more weeks of reinforcement learning since the preview made Mistral Large 4 the best open-weight model for coding. It reports a lead score of 19.7% on Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark and 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, up 13 percentage points from the preview. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral reports a 48% score, effectively tied with GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task; a Hugging Face post on the release lists 49.8% for the same index.

Mistral is pitching the model for defensive cybersecurity. The company reports a 51% score on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and an average 96.6% refusal rate on malicious cyber requests, the highest it measured among open models. Hugging Face's post says the model scores 82% on that index's task of reproducing and then patching a real vulnerability. Mistral also wrote that, after watching live traffic since the preview, it sees a potential for the model to help with real attacks and is changing its guardrails.

According to Hugging Face, the model is a mixture-of-experts design with a 1-million-token context window, released in FP8 and NVFP4 versions with day-one support in Transformers, vLLM and llama.cpp. Mistral lists API pricing of $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens, and says the model is also available through Microsoft Foundry and NVIDIA-hosted endpoints.

stories.title: Genie 4, DeepMind's real-time world model, now generates sound and uses Gemini as a planner
paragraphs: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers, MarkTechPost reports. The world model generates explorable environments from text and image prompts in real time, frame by frame, and users move with keyboard controls and steer events with plain-language prompts.

It is DeepMind's first real-time world model to generate audio natively, producing ambient sound, music and character dialogue together with the visuals. A Gemini model runs inside the simulation loop as a planner and keeps the scene progressing between user inputs, which DeepMind describes as an early step toward hybrid world models.

DeepMind released no benchmark tables. It says Genie 4 should come soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie, followed by early-access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, and that all of its video and audio carry SynthID watermarks.

stories.title: Anthropic expands its AI for Science program, giving Claude credits to 20 foundations, institutes and research projects
paragraphs: Anthropic announced on Oct. 28, 2026, that it is expanding its AI for Science program, which gives free Claude credits to researchers on high-impact scientific projects, by partnering with 20 scientific foundations, institutions and research groups around the world. The company says it started the program in May 2025 and has since supported hundreds of projects across biology, medicine, physics, chemistry, climate science and mathematics, and launched a discounted Team plan for scientists.

Six funders and societies will pass Claude credits on to researchers, according to Anthropic: the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, the Simons Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, the Open Source for Science Fund at Renaissance Philanthropy, the U.S. National Science Foundation, and CAS, a division of the American Chemical Society. Six research institutions will use the credits internally: the Space Telescope Science Institute, which runs science operations for the Hubble, Webb and Roman space telescopes; the Wellcome Sanger Institute; the Francis Crick Institute; Imperial College London's Department of Life Sciences; EMBL; and the Gladstone Institutes.

Anthropic is also funding specific projects directly: FlyWire at Princeton, which produced the first complete wiring map of an adult fruit fly's brain; Columbia's LEAP climate-modeling center; AstroPath at Johns Hopkins, which images tumors cell by cell using methods from astronomy; the gnomAD genetic variation database at the Broad Institute; Tau Ceti, a community project building a library of mathematics checked by computer in the Lean language; and Australia's Centre for Population Genomics.

The company says it has already partnered with HHMI Janelia Research Campus on the Model Hardware Standard, a shared specification for letting AI agents safely operate lab instruments that is in research preview, and supports the Allen Institute's work on teams of AI agents for analyzing brain, cell and immune-system data. Anthropic says many of the new projects will produce public goods such as open datasets, open-source software and open standards, and that most of the collaborations are still in early stages.
